Fiserv is hiring an Android Application Framework Developer - Device Engineering for its Device Engineering team. The role develops Android framework services and integrates software with POS hardware peripherals, while managing USB and network communications and troubleshooting device issues.
Finance
FinTech
Information Technology
Payments
Financial Services
Information Services
No H1B
Responsibilities
Develop Android application framework services and background daemons in Kotlin and Java that interface directly with external hardware and microcontrollers
Integrate third-party vendor SDKs and write communication pipelines for POS peripherals, including receipt printers, barcode scanners, cash drawers, and weight scales
Utilize Android USB Host (OTG) APIs to manage hardware attach/detach lifecycle events, configure dynamic USB permissions, and implement socket programming for network IP printers
Use command-line tools (adb, Logcat, packet/serial sniffers) to isolate, reproduce, and debug hardware integration bugs and OS regressions across our terminal fleet
Collaborate with senior engineers to explore Android Open Source Project (AOSP) internals, framework extensions, and custom device services
Leverage modern AI-assisted engineering tools (such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and coding agents) to accelerate development, refactor framework code, and optimize debugging workflows

Required
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical & Computer Engineering (ECE), Computer Science, or a related discipline (Graduating seniors or recent grads welcome)
Demonstrated classroom, capstone, research lab, or personal project experience building software that talks to physical devices or external hardware (e.g., IoT devices, Arduino/Raspberry Pi, robotics, microcontrollers, USB accessories, or sensor integration)
Strong foundational coding skills in Java or Kotlin, with working knowledge or academic exposure to C or C++
Practical understanding of native Android development fundamentals (Activities, Services, BroadcastReceivers, Intents, and background threading)
Academic or practical familiarity with low-level communication concepts such as TCP/UDP socket programming, USB device communication (Host/OTG), or serial/UART protocols
Rock-solid grasp of core computer science fundamentals: Object-Oriented Design, Data Structures, Operating Systems (threading, processes, memory management), and Git version control
High curiosity, passion for device hardware, and excitement to learn POS platform architecture and payment security standards
You must currently possess valid and unrestricted U.S. work authorization to be considered for this role. Individuals with temporary visas including, but not limited to, F-1 (OPT, CPT, STEM), H-1B, H-2, or TN, or any candidate requiring sponsorship, now or in the future, will not be considered for this role
Preferred
Familiarity with the Android USB Host API (android.hardware.usb) or managing hardware permissions and USB intent filters
Coursework or project exposure to the Android Open Source Project (AOSP) or building custom Android ROMs/firmware
Hands-on experience integrating third-party vendor hardware SDKs or libraries
Exposure to low-level microcontroller communication (SPI, I2C, UART) or embedded Linux environments
Benefits

Paid holidays and generous time away policies
No-cost mental health support through Employee Assistance Programs
Living Proof program to recognize your peers’ extra effort with points redeemable for rewards
Eight Employee Resource Groups to foster a collaborative culture and expand your network
Unparalleled professional growth with training, development, and internal mobility opportunities
Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance options available from day one
Retirement planning and discounted shares with the Employee Stock Purchase Plan
Tuition assistance and reimbursement program
Paid parental, caregiver, and military leave
